_: The one run the landing page prints in full.
`input` is the request the page describes in words; `verified` is what the
engine returned for it. Neither half is edited by hand: run
`node scripts/verify-worked-example.mjs --write` and take what the engine says.
`pnpm check` runs the same script without --write and fails if the page has
drifted, which it silently had — see the header of that script.

formulas.bandB: tower plate 1280.00 m² × 13 level(s) of floor area (14 under the height ceiling, less 1 given to parking)
formulas.bandC: 100 unit(s) supportable by parking × 96.77 m² GFA per unit

formulas.levels: floor(min(13 level(s) of floor area, smallest band 9677.42 m² ÷ tower plate 1280.00 m²))

notAssessed: The ring aisle is the ramp: it climbs one 3.2 m storey over one 112.46 m lap, 2.85%, within the 4% a floor with parked cars on it may fall (DBC B.7.2.3.1, Figure B.55). No ramp strip is needed.
Of the 205 m² reserved for plant and circulation, 185 m² is drawn on the island in 4 piece(s) and 19 m² has no room on it at all. The deduction is still charged in full against the bay count.

Bays stand against all four walls and one 6 m ring aisle serves them: 22 to each long wall and 4 to each short one, less the 0 the way in and the core take. The island the ring encloses is 32.86 × 11.37 m.

Laid out as bays to the walls, the ring aisle sloped as the ramp: 52 bays, against 37 modules along the width; 24 modules along the depth; 0 bays to the walls, one ring aisle (a straight ramp climbing a 3.2 m storey needs 6.30 × 30.27 m (DBC Tables B.9 and B.10), reached from the ring at one end of the island, and the 32.86 × 11.37 m island does not have it clear of the core), on the same level. All 4 were packed.

The 288 m² deducted for cores, plant and the ramp landing costs about 13 bays at 21.25 m² each — the area one more bay takes inside a module, not the gross area per bay. Of it, 83 m² is the core, standing where it is drawn (0 bay(s) were not placed there), and 205 m² is the strip reserved at the edge.

Headroom (Table B.9, 2.4 m clear above any point of a ramp): the ramps stand in one strip on every level, so over each is the next, one 3.20 m storey up. The slab, its beams and anything hung below them over the ramp may be at most 0.80 m deep. No structure is drawn: this is the budget a design must fit in, not a statement that one does.
Whether a T junction sits opposite the chosen opening (B.7.2.1: "Vehicle access shall not be located opposite a T junction"). That needs the surrounding road network, which no affection plan carries.
RTA approval. B.7.2.1 defers the location to RTA requirements and the Dubai access management manual; nothing here substitutes for that.
Whether a traffic impact study is required for this development.

parkingInFar.verdict: The parking-in-FAR treatment moves regulatory capacity by 5367 m², but not the governing capacity: the parking limit binds below both treatments. On this plot the open regulatory question does not change the answer — though it would on a plot where the FAR ceiling binds.

workbookSheets.name: Capacity
workbookSheets.note: Three bands, never merged and never averaged. There is no "realistic" or "expected" figure in this file because the engine does not produce one — the honest substitute is the user realism discount, which defaults to 1.00.

workbookSheets.name: Parking demand
workbookSheets.note: Demand at the probe target. Compare against the "Parking level" sheet: a level that packs fewer bays than this sheet requires is a real and reportable state, not an error in either number.

workbookSheets.name: GFA calculation
workbookSheets.note: Allowed is FAR × plot area, before the parking-in-FAR treatment. Proposed is whole floors of the tower plate, plus parking only where it counts toward FAR. The residential and commercial allowances are capped separately and summed at the end. Statements with no figure — an allowance nobody stated, a floor named and not counted — are below the table, not in the value column.

workbookSheets.name: Parking level
workbookSheets.note: Bays placed as rectangles to Dubai Building Code Table B.11, not an area divided by a factor. A bay count that cannot be laid out is not a bay count.

workbookSheets.name: Assumption register
workbookSheets.note: Every gap the engine filled, why it filled it that way, and what the answer does if the assumption is wrong. Ranked by effect.

Generated capacity study, not a submission drawing.
notModelled: No column is drawn, and so no grid bubbles: the layout places no column, and a bubble is read as a column line. Bays are packed side by side at Table B.11's 2.50 m. Its additional 300 mm for a bay bounded by a structural element or a wall is not charged anywhere, beside a column or at the end of a run against a wall, so where a wall or a column stops a car door opening the count is more than a drawn structure would allow. NOT ASSESSED. Position on a parking sheet is given by bay number and by the dimensioned module.
Stairs and lifts as rooms, and plant. The run declares how much of each parking level they take — drawn as the reserved zone — not where each one goes.
Slab thickness. Levels are planes at their floor level. The engine computes no slab depth, and a drawn thickness would be an invented one.
Façades, windows, balconies and units. The engine computes none of them.

Neighbouring buildings and the road. The run knows which edges of the plot face a road and which face a neighbour — the site plan writes that on the boundary — but not what stands beyond them, so neither is drawn.

Escape distances and the pedestrian route from the street to the entrance — NOT ASSESSED. The fire code's travel distance, common path and dead-end limits (Table 3.6A) are declared in the deferred-check list; no floor plan is drawn to measure them on.
Bicycle parking — NOT ASSESSED. DBC B.7.2.7 asks for bicycle parking equal to a twentieth of the car parking requirement, within 30 m of the building entrance; no bicycle space is counted or drawn.

Clear height on the parking levels. Each is drawn 3.20 m floor to floor, a placeholder storey height that no instrument prints, and DBC Table B.4 asks 2.30 m clear for light-vehicle parking, measured to the underside of the lowest beam or soffit. That leaves 0.90 m for the slab, beams and services, which are not computed, so whether it is enough is NOT ASSESSED.

The sloped ring is drawn level in 3D and in section. On plan the ring aisle and the bays on it climb one storey over each 112.46 m lap; the 3D view and the sections stand every parking level flat at its floor height, and where the core door meets the ring at each level is not drawn.

The core, as a design. Its outline is the tower plate scaled to the core area, and only that area is a computed quantity. The stairs, lifts and lobby drawn inside it, and the door into it at ground level, are an indicative layout, assumed: egress, lift traffic and fire-fighting are NOT ASSESSED, no riser or core wall is placed, and no route from the street to the core's door is drawn.

The ground floor, as a services design. Every room in its reserved strip whose width is a typical figure is an assumption: it is not sized, ventilated or access-checked against any requirement. The substation is sized from DEWA §11.4.1, and the LV room is drawn beside it (§11.2.3) at a typical width; neither is ventilated or access-checked — §11.5.1 is only partly mechanizable and is NOT ASSESSED. The garbage room and the water tank are sized by the Dubai Building Code, and this run does not apply it: B.8.5.2.3 sizes waste storage for two days of waste at a suggested 12 kg for each 100 m² of net area for residential use, with containers by Table B.29, and H.5.5.3 sizes a domestic water tank on 24 hours of demand at Table H.6's rates. Where they are drawn it is at a typical width, and their size against those clauses is NOT ASSESSED. GARBAGE ROOM: GARBAGE ROOM needs 4.00 m along the strip and 2.43 m of its 8.43 m is left, so it was not drawn rather than drawn narrow.

Clear height, in conflict. The substation is drawn on a ground storey of 3.20 m floor to floor, and DEWA §11.2.5 and DBC G.7.2.3 ask a single-room substation at ground floor for at least 3.70 m clear height — more than the whole storey, before any slab or services are taken off it. The two cannot both stand: the ground storey has to be taller, or the substation split, with its RMU room at 3.0 m clear. Neither change is made here; the storey height and the levels above it are as computed.
The refuse room is not drawn on this run, and its size against DBC B.8.5.2.3 and Table B.29 is NOT ASSESSED.
